subject: Geography
description: Major lakes of India: location, type (saltwater, glacial, etc.)

questions.stem: INDIA's LARGEST lake by area, a SALTWATER coastal lagoon, is:

options.option_text: Wular Lake, Kashmir's largest
Chilika Lake, Odisha's coastal lagoon
Sambhar Lake, of Rajasthan area
Loktak Lake, of Manipur state

questions.explanation: CHILIKA LAKE — Odisha's east coast. India's largest BRACKISH (slightly salty) coastal lagoon (~1100 sq km), and Asia's largest brackish lagoon. RAMSAR site (1981, India's first). Famous for: migratory birds (~150 species), Irrawaddy DOLPHINS. Source of livelihood for thousands of fishermen. SAMBHAR (Rajasthan) — India's largest INLAND saltwater lake, source of salt. WULAR (Kashmir) — India's largest FRESHWATER lake. LOKTAK (Manipur) — famous for unique floating PHUMDIS, home to endangered SANGAI deer.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: WULAR LAKE, India's LARGEST FRESHWATER lake, is in:

options.option_text: Himachal Pradesh, in the lower hills
Jammu and Kashmir (Bandipore district)
Uttarakhand, in the Garhwal region
Sikkim, in the eastern Himalayan area

questions.explanation: WULAR LAKE — north of Srinagar, in BANDIPORE district of Jammu + Kashmir. Largest freshwater lake in India (~125-200 sq km, varying with season). Fed by JHELUM river. RAMSAR site (1990). Important for Kashmir's fish supply. Other Kashmir lakes: DAL (boat-houses, shikara rides — Srinagar's most famous), NAGIN (close to Dal), MANASBAL (small, deepest in Kashmir). Distractor 1 — HP has Renuka, Bhrigu, Chandratal lakes. Distractor 3 — Uttarakhand has Naini, Bhimtal, Sat Tal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: VEMBANAD LAKE, India's longest lake, runs through which state?

options.option_text: Karnataka, with the Tungabhadra river
Kerala (Kochi backwaters region)
Tamil Nadu, with Cauvery delta lakes
Andhra Pradesh, with Pulicat lake

questions.explanation: VEMBANAD — India's LONGEST lake (~96 km) and largest by area in Kerala. Runs through Alappuzha, Kottayam, Ernakulam districts in Kerala. Forms part of KERALA BACKWATERS (network of brackish lagoons + lakes). Houseboat tourism centre. Vembanad Bird Sanctuary; KUMARAKOM is on its banks. Famous SNAKE BOAT RACE (Nehru Trophy) held annually in Aug-Sep at Punnamada, near Alappuzha. RAMSAR site (2002). PULICAT LAKE (Andhra-TN border) = India's 2nd largest brackish lagoon (after Chilika). KOLLERU (AP, freshwater, between Krishna + Godavari deltas). OOTY's lake is small.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: SAMBHAR Salt Lake, India's largest inland saltwater lake, is in:

options.option_text: Gujarat (around the Gulf of Kutch)
Rajasthan (near city of Jaipur)
Maharashtra (the Lonar lake area)
Tamil Nadu (Pulicat-Bay area)

questions.explanation: SAMBHAR LAKE — RAJASTHAN, near Jaipur. India's largest INLAND saltwater lake (~190 sq km in monsoon, much smaller in summer). Major SALT producer (Sambhar salt — accounts for ~9% of India's salt). RAMSAR site (1990). Migratory FLAMINGOS — major attraction. LONAR LAKE (Maharashtra) — formed by METEOR IMPACT (~50,000 years ago); both saline + alkaline. PUSHKAR LAKE (Rajasthan, also) — sacred Hindu pilgrimage; only Brahma temple in India nearby.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: LOKTAK LAKE, the largest freshwater lake in NE India, is famous for:

options.option_text: Ice-skating in winter season events
Floating circular phumdis + Sangai deer
World's largest commercial fish farms
Oil drilling rigs on the lake surface

questions.explanation: LOKTAK LAKE — Manipur. Unique 'PHUMDIS' — circular floating mats of vegetation + organic matter, on which fishermen live. KEIBUL LAMJAO NATIONAL PARK (within the lake) — only floating national park in the world. Home to the SANGAI / 'dancing deer' (Rucervus eldii eldii) — endangered, state animal of Manipur, found only here. Loktak source of HYDROPOWER (Loktak Hydel Project). RAMSAR site (1990); also added to Montreux Record (degraded condition).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: DAL LAKE, with its famous shikaras + houseboats, is in:

options.option_text: Shimla, Himachal hill capital
Srinagar, Kashmir's summer capital
Nainital, in the Kumaon region
Mussoorie, popular in Uttarakhand

questions.explanation: DAL LAKE — in SRINAGAR, J&K. Famous for SHIKARAS (gondola-like wooden boats) + HOUSEBOATS (originally a way for visitors to stay during British era when British were not allowed to own land in princely Kashmir). Surrounded by Mughal gardens (Nishat, Shalimar, Chashme Shahi). FLOATING vegetable gardens — a Kashmir innovation. Lake size shrinking due to encroachment + pollution; major restoration efforts ongoing. Distractors are all hill stations but with smaller / less iconic lakes.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: PANGONG TSO, the high-altitude blue lake in news for the 2020 India-China standoff, lies in:

options.option_text: Sikkim, the eastern Himalayas
Ladakh (between India + China)
Arunachal Pradesh (NE state)
Uttarakhand (Garhwal Himalayas)

questions.explanation: PANGONG TSO ('Tso' = lake) — high altitude (~4350 m / 14,270 ft) endorheic lake in LADAKH UT. ~135 km long, narrow (~5 km wide); ~60% in CHINA (Tibet) + ~40% in INDIA. Brackish/saline despite being high. Famous striking BLUE colour. Setting of '3 Idiots' film (climactic ending). 2020 PANGONG-TSO standoff — India + China troops clashed at northern bank, leading to Galwan Valley clash. Disengagement after months of negotiations. NEAR: SO MORIRI (also Ladakh, freshwater); TSO KAR (smaller). Distractor 1 — Sikkim has Tsomgo (Changu) Lake.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Chilika Lake in Odisha was India's first wetland to receive a Ramsar (Wetlands of International Importance) designation. In which year did this designation occur?

options.option_text: 1975 — the year the Ramsar Convention on Wetlands itself entered into force
1981 — placing Chilika among the first Ramsar sites designated in Asia
1990 — after the Indian Parliament formally ratified the Ramsar Convention
2002 — when Chilika was removed from the Montreux Record of threatened sites

questions.explanation: India ratified the Ramsar Convention in 1981 and simultaneously designated Chilika Lake as its first Ramsar Wetland, making it one of the earliest in Asia. 1975 is when the Convention itself entered into force internationally, not when India joined. 2002 is a key Chilika date but marks when Chilika was removed from the Montreux Record (a list of Ramsar sites under threat), not when it was originally designated.

questions.stem: Kolleru Lake, declared a Wildlife Sanctuary in 1999 and a Ramsar site in 2002, is a natural freshwater lake fed by seasonal drainage from which pair of river systems?

options.option_text: Mahanadi and Brahmani river deltas in coastal Odisha state
Tungabhadra and Krishna river deltas in Telangana state
Krishna and Godavari river deltas in Andhra Pradesh state
Cauvery and Vaigai river deltas in coastal Tamil Nadu state

questions.explanation: Kolleru Lake lies in West Godavari and Krishna districts of Andhra Pradesh, nestled between the deltas of the Krishna (to the south) and Godavari (to the north), which feed it through natural drainage channels. Option B is wrong because Telangana has no significant coastal delta region. Option A points to Odisha's Mahanadi-Brahmani system, which has no connection to Kolleru.

questions.stem: Pulicat Lake, India's second-largest brackish water lagoon, is separated from the Bay of Bengal by a narrow barrier island. Which major Indian space facility is situated on that barrier island?

options.option_text: Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station (TERLS) in Kerala
Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SHAR) on Sriharikota Island
National Remote Sensing Centre (NRSC) at Hyderabad campus
Vikram Sarabhai Space Centre (VSSC) in Thiruvananthapuram

questions.explanation: Sriharikota, the barrier island separating Pulicat Lake from the Bay of Bengal, is home to the Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC SHAR — Sriharikota High Altitude Range), India's primary orbital launch facility. TERLS (Thumba) and VSSC are both in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala — a common point of confusion for candidates. NRSC is a remote sensing data centre in Hyderabad, not a launch site.

questions.stem: Lonar Lake in Buldhana district, Maharashtra is one of only four known impact-generated saline lakes in the world. What makes its origin geologically exceptional?

options.option_text: A volcanic caldera formed when the Deccan Traps basaltic surface collapsed inward
A tectonic graben depression filled by seasonal drainage from the Godavari basin
A hypervelocity meteorite-impact crater lake with saline-alkaline water chemistry
A glacial cirque lake formed during Pleistocene glaciation over the Deccan plateau

questions.explanation: Lonar Lake formed roughly 50,000 years ago when a meteorite struck the Deccan Traps basalt at hypervelocity, creating a circular crater now filled with saline-alkaline water (pH ~10.5). Option A is the most tempting distractor: Deccan Traps basalt IS the surrounding rock, but that makes Lonar unusual (impacts in basalt are rare), not a volcanic caldera. Pleistocene glaciation of the Deccan plateau (D) never occurred.

questions.stem: Tsomgo (Changu) Lake in East Sikkim requires all non-local visitors, including citizens from other Indian states, to obtain a Protected Area Permit (PAP) before visiting. What is the primary statutory reason for this restriction?

options.option_text: Located at over 3,700 m in a Protected Area bordering China-held territory
A notified Wildlife Sanctuary where human entry disturbs migratory bird nesting
A sacred Buddhist site managed exclusively under a Sikkim monastery trust
A primary source for Gangtok's municipal water supply requiring sanitation controls

questions.explanation: Tsomgo Lake lies within a Protected/Restricted Area in East Sikkim, close to the Nathu La pass on the India-China border. Under the PAP system, proximity to a sensitive international border — not wildlife protection or religious management — triggers the permit requirement for all non-residents. Option B is a common trap: Tsomgo is not a notified Wildlife Sanctuary. Option C overstates the monastery's legal authority over access.

questions.stem: Ashtamudi Lake in Kollam, Kerala (Ramsar 2002) takes its name from the Malayalam for 'eight-armed', reflecting its multi-pronged shape. Which traditional economic activity, conducted directly in the lake's brackish water, has been flagged in Ramsar conservation documentation for oxygen depletion?

options.option_text: Prawn aquaculture using cage systems anchored along the lake's eight arms
Traditional cheena vala (Chinese lift-net) fishing practised on the lakeshore
Handloom weaving using kalamkari natural dyes prepared with the lake's water
Coir-fibre retting, where coconut husks are soaked in the brackish lake water

questions.explanation: Coir retting — soaking coconut husks in water to loosen fibres — is a centuries-old Kollam industry conducted directly in Ashtamudi Lake. Husk decomposition depletes dissolved oxygen and releases tannins, raising water-quality concerns documented by Ramsar authorities. Chinese lift-nets (cheena vala) are famously associated with Fort Kochi and Vembanad Lake, not Ashtamudi. Kalamkari is a textile art from Andhra Pradesh, making Option C a geography-mismatch trap.

questions.stem: Manasbal Lake in Ganderbal district, J&K, has been called 'the supreme gem of all Kashmir lakes'. Which pairing of physical and ecological distinctions correctly sets it apart from Dal and Wular?

options.option_text: It is the sole Kashmir lake with a documented freshwater pearl mussel population
It is the deepest lake in the Kashmir valley, famous for dense Nelumbo lotus bloom
It is the highest-altitude lake in J&K still navigable by shikara year-round
It is the southernmost Ramsar Wetland in the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir

questions.explanation: Manasbal Lake (~5 km²) reaches approximately 13 m depth — far deeper than Dal Lake (avg ~1.5 m) or Wular (avg ~3–5 m) — earning it the title of deepest lake in the Kashmir valley. It is also renowned for its summer Nelumbo nucifera (sacred lotus) bloom. Option D is a deliberate trap: Manasbal is NOT a Ramsar site; Wular Lake and Hokera Wetland hold that status in J&K. Option C misattributes the high-altitude shikara-navigable distinction, which better fits Tsomgo in Sikkim.
